title: What does DelegateSet do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of DelegateSet and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, DelegateSet grants, changes or revokes another account's permission to submit specified transactions on the owner's behalf. [1]

Permissions are recorded in a Delegate entry rather than by handing over a signing secret. The reference warns about PaymentBurn granular permission before fixCleanup3_4_0: it can also permit minting in certain circumstances. Least privilege therefore depends on the target network's fixes as well as the named permission. [1]

The DelegateSet reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using DelegateSet, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
